task.title: Fail durable workflow runs with exact diagnostics
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/708 under decision https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/707 by persisting caller-owned unsuccessful outcomes separately from cancellation and authored terminal topology.
acceptance_criteria: Validate and preserve one non-empty exact caller diagnostic for an active or paused non-terminal workflow run.
Require the caller-observed revision and persist exact current-phase provenance without changing immutable topology or phase.
Make failure a distinct terminal lifecycle condition that rejects every later mutation while preserving pause-at-failure evidence.
Expose failure through exact load, deterministic list, and typed history while rejecting malformed, impossible, duplicate, or post-failure evidence fail closed.

attempts.diagnostic: The focused workflow-run target failed because the failure value, store mutation, projected state, and typed history variant did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added tests for active and paused failure, exact diagnostics and revisions, stale and invalid states, every post-failure guard, reopen, list, history, malformed provenance, and invalid event ordering.

attempts.diagnostic: A separate failure event preserved the distinction between unsuccessful work, intentional cancellation, and arrival at authored terminal topology without inferring external causes.
attempts.patch: Added validated failure diagnostics, exact-revision fail mutation, terminal guards, strict replay and history projection, ADR-0015, and milestone documentation.

attempts.summary: Preserved the bounded failure contract through review.
attempts.diagnostic: Independent review found no blocking correctness, integrity, scope, or documentation issue, and CodeRabbit reviewed the exact implementation head before merge.
attempts.patch: Kept automatic detection, retries, recovery, compensation, execution binding, and scheduling outside the verified caller-evidence slice.

outcome.summary: Durable workflow runs now represent exact caller-owned failure as a distinct terminal lifecycle outcome with strict replay and preserved paused-state evidence.

lessons: Failure, cancellation, and authored terminal arrival are separate lifecycle semantics and should not be encoded through one another.
Phase-preserving terminal events still need exact phase provenance so replay can reject impossible histories.
Failure while paused must preserve the pause marker because clearing it would invent an unrecorded resume.
Exact revisions serialize caller failure intent against every other lifecycle mutation without unsafe retry.
Caller-owned failure evidence does not detect causes, execute actions, retry, recover, compensate, schedule, or grant permission.
